meaning: to make more effort than is expected or required
literal_translation: докладати додаткових зусиль, щоб зробити щось краще, ніж вимагається
example: She went the extra mile to finish her project on time.
origin: Often linked to the idea of walking one mile beyond what is required; the exact origin is unclear

wrong_meanings.meaning: to walk a long distance on foot
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal reading of the words, but the idiom has no physical meaning about walking.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish a task earlier than planned
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about extra effort, not about speed or finishing early.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse to help other people
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes doing more than expected, so it is the opposite of refusing to help.

explanation: 'Go the extra mile' means to do more than people expect, usually to help someone or to achieve a good result. It is common in work and school contexts.
